content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Central set Q is mis-defined as primes dividing A; the whole argument only works (and is elsewhere stated by the author) for Q = all primes \u2264 A.", "errors": [{"description": "Q is defined as the primes dividing A, but every subsequent use requires Q = {primes \u2264 A}: e.g. 'if all prime factors of x are at most A then \u03c3(x)=P(x)' and 'every prime in P(x)\\\u03c3(x) is greater than A' both fail for Q={p|A} (A=15, x=18: \u03c3(18)={3} is not good). Consequently L=\u220f_{p|A}p is also wrong (A=15 gives L=15, but 33 is not a term while 18 is). The author's own 'Hypotheses tested' section states the correct set, so it is a one-line repairable typo.", "quote": "Q=\\{p:p\\text{ is prime and }p\\mid A\\},\n\\qquad\n\\sigma(x)=P(x)\\cap Q."}], "notes": "With Q read as all primes \u2264 A, the argument is coherent and complete: characterization (1), the descent construction Rp^k with the minimal-counterexample b, upward-closedness, and the counting of terms in (a_n, a_n+L] are all correct and carefully handled from n=1."}
